clue.text: A local politician accustomed to being denounced

parts.note: CC is a county councillor, a British local politician
used, as in used to something, means accustomed

explanation.surface: A councillor who has grown used to being publicly denounced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to being' is link material; 'accustomed' reads as part of the phrase 'accustomed to', but on its own it gives USED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be charged with wrongdoing is to be publicly blamed, so the charged person is denounced.

clue.text: United around Tory immediately

indicators.note: around tells us the word for united wraps itself about the letter for Tory

parts.note: at one means united or in agreement
C stands for Conservative, the Tory party

explanation.surface: A coalition forming around a Tory without delay.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means straight away, without any delay.

clue.text: Weep about a woman taking crack

indicators.note: about signals the word for weep goes round the woman's name

parts.note: cry means weep
Ann is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Someone sobbing over a woman taking cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is a link word; 'crack' looks like the drug but is a narrow gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A small narrow gap or chink in a wall is a nook of this kind.

clue.text: Diplomacy to keep the Royal Yacht?

explanation.surface: A diplomatic argument for retaining the Royal Yacht.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the punning sense: the Royal Yacht Britannia was literally a craft of the state.
explanation.definitionFit: The art of governing and managing foreign affairs is diplomacy; a vessel owned by the state is, punningly, a state vessel.

clue.text: To plunge into water is the same function

parts.note: do is short for ditto, meaning the same
use means function or purpose

explanation.surface: A remark that ducking in water serves the same purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word; DO, from ditto, is a crossword convention for 'the same'.
explanation.definitionFit: Drenching or submerging something is plunging it into water.

clue.text: Being able to pay is beneficial

explanation.surface: A remark that solvency does you good.
explanation.definitionFit: A debtor who can settle is creditworthy for the sum; something that helps you is good for you, wholesome.

clue.text: Where one may be questioned and fed

definitions.text: Where one may be questioned and fed

parts.words: Where one may be questioned and fed
parts.note: to grill is to interrogate, yet it is also a way of cooking; the place is a restaurant serving cooked meats

explanation.surface: A place of interrogation that also feeds its suspects.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant specialising in grilled food is where diners are fed, while 'grill' also means question hard.

clue.text: Unwilling to be beheaded for blasphemy

indicators.note: beheaded means the word for unwilling loses its first letter

parts.note: loath means unwilling or reluctant

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant to be executed for blasphemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' removes L, the first letter of LOATH; 'to be' and 'for' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A profane curse or swear word is blasphemy in the looser sense.

clue.text: Disgusting drama of unsporting behaviour

parts.note: foul means disgusting
a play is a drama

explanation.surface: A nasty theatrical piece about cheating in sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheating or breaking the rules in a game is unsporting behaviour; it also means criminal violence.

clue.text: Elected to be sent back

explanation.surface: A politician voted in only to be sent home again.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate voted into office is said to be brought back to Parliament; anything posted back has been sent back.

clue.text: Old radio buff returned to a US city

indicators.note: returned means the word for radio buff is read backwards

parts.note: a ham is an amateur radio enthusiast

explanation.surface: An elderly radio enthusiast returning to an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns HAM into MAH; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebraska's largest city sits on the Missouri River.

clue.text: An investment that gives one confidence

parts.note: a unit is one single thing
trust means confidence

explanation.surface: An investment advertised as reassuring.
explanation.definitionFit: A pooled fund in which investors buy shares is a type of investment.

clue.text: Nell cried brokenly at first, poor little thing

indicators.note: brokenly says the letters of Nell cried are broken up and rearranged
first picks the opening letter of the word at

explanation.surface: Little Nell sobbing pitifully about a poor child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brokenly' rearranges NELLCRIED into CINDERELL; 'at first' gives the A of 'at'.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy-tale heroine is the poor neglected drudge, hence any overlooked person.

clue.text: Some seditious paramilitary units fight

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Rebel paramilitary units engaged in combat.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'units fight' was wrong: the answer means fight alone, and 'units' is surface padding acting as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To box or argue is to exchange blows or words, a sense of fight.

clue.text: Be explicit, and charm one solicitor

parts.note: a spell is a charm
I is the Roman numeral one
a tout is someone who solicits custom

explanation.surface: Bewitch a lawyer and be plain about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' looks like the lawyer, but here it is someone who solicits, a tout; 'and' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain something in the plainest terms is to be explicit.

clue.text: Prominent position for Longleat lions?

explanation.surface: The best spot at a safari park reserved for its lions.
explanation.walkthrough: Longleat is an English stately home with a famous safari park; a group of lions is a pride. 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The most honoured place is a prominent position; a group of lions housed in a particular spot is literally that.

clue.text: They dared foolishly to run low on water

indicators.note: foolishly suggests the letters of They dared are rearranged in a silly way

explanation.surface: Reckless people risking going without water.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose too much bodily fluid is to run short of water.

clue.text: Stop meetings with professional criminal

parts.note: pro is short for professional
a rogue is a criminal or rascal

explanation.surface: Professional crook breaking up meetings.
explanation.definitionFit: To discontinue a session of Parliament without dissolving it is to halt its meetings.

clue.text: Where film is loaded away from view

explanation.surface: A secret spot for loading film.
explanation.definitionFit: Film sits inside a camera; a court hearing held privately is away from public view.

clue.text: Everyday freedom enjoyed by the Tulliver children

definitions.text: freedom enjoyed by the Tulliver children

explanation.surface: The daily liberty of children in a George Eliot novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom and Maggie Tulliver grow up at Dorlcote Mill in George Eliot's 'The Mill on the Floss', so they had free rein there.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ordinary is everyday; having the run of a place means free access to it.

clue.text: A material supplied whenever one wants

parts.note: twill is a woven fabric

explanation.surface: A cloth handed out whenever wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something as and when you like is acting freely, as desired.

clue.text: Cheery, despite having the wind up

explanation.surface: Staying cheerful while frightened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having the wind up' is British slang for being scared, but here it is read literally as windy weather; 'despite' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright, carefree manner is cheery; a day with a stiff wind blowing is literally windy.

clue.text: Stern parent

explanation.surface: A strict mother or father.
explanation.definitionFit: The back of a ship is its stern; to parent a child is to bring it up.

clue.text: These days a cleric has to supervise

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era
a minister is a cleric

explanation.surface: A modern priest obliged to take charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage or run affairs is to supervise them.

clue.text: That is to be written out in full

definitions.text: That is to be written out in full

parts.words: That is to be written out in full
parts.note: the abbreviation i.e., meaning that is, expanded into its full Latin words

explanation.surface: An instruction that some text be written out in full.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is the unabbreviated form of i.e., which means that is.

clue.text: Cease street work

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A demand that roadworks be halted.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt or come to an end is to cease.

clue.text: Enraged at being mauled by hound

indicators.note: mauled means the letters of Enraged at are torn about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Angry at being savaged by a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A very large breed of dog, so a kind of hound.

clue.text: Arch appeal for charitable donations

parts.note: O, an exclamation, is an appeal or plea
to give is to make charitable donations

explanation.surface: A charity appeal asking for money.
explanation.walkthrough: A plea reading 'O give!' sounds like a charity appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointed Gothic arch is an architectural term for this shape.

clue.text: eg Retired redcaps surrounded by drink

parts.note: ex means former, so retired

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the redcaps inside the word for drink

parts.note: ale is a drink
redcaps are British military police, MP

explanation.surface: Retired military police surrounded by drink, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: Redcaps is British slang for the Royal Military Police, who wear red caps.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation eg means for instance, introducing a sample case.

clue.text: To agree without reservations

parts.note: to tally is to agree or correspond

explanation.surface: Agreeing wholeheartedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Completely, entirely, with no holding back.
